profile.name: Jiyan
profile.introduction: Jiyan, leader of the Midnight Rangers, acts with swift and resolute righteousness. He possesses the formidable ability to conjure a powerful Qingloong from the winds, making him invincible on the battlefield.
profile.review:
Jiyan is a 5-star Aero main damage dealer and was the first Main DPS as well as first limited character to ever exist in the game. His kit is definitely reminiscent of the philosophy of the game’s on-release days, not centred around any specific game mechanics other than dealing as much damage as possible within his Ultimate damage window, and general Heavy Attack-related buffs.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

Jiyan’s rotation revolves around his Ultimate almost entirely. This is because his Ultimate makes him enter a special stance called Qingloong mode for 10s. In those 10s, he is able to cast special Qingloong Heavy Attacks, which deal way more damage than anything else in his kit. They represent the core of his damage and fitting in as many as he can in that 10s window is the goal of his rotation.

Jiyan’s Forte is built up through his Intro or Basic Attacks. He holds up to 2 charges of “Resolve” (60 points, 30 per charge) that empower either his Skills or Ultimates when consumed. The increase on the empowered Skill is really minimal though, so what matters is the Ultimate. When cast, it deals no damage unless Jiyan holds a charge of Resolve, in which case he performs an opening attack that deals a good amount of damage. Jiyan also gains the enhancement on his Skill for free if he casts it during his Ultimate window.

Finally, Jiyan’s passives are simple damage increases activated by Intro and hitting a target respectively, and his Outro enables him to cast 2 Coordinated Attacks for a bit more damage when other characters cast Heavy Attacks for 8s. Most of the time, this will only be triggered once per team rotation, though it’s possible to go out of your way to trigger it a second time if you want.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Jiyan has been an outdated DPS for a long time. It’s fair to say that as a 1;x DPS, much like the other older members of the roster, he should not even be considered to pull if you care about the meta. His teams deal too little damage to be worth it, or require insane time/build investment to learn proper rotations with a good build. Generally, Jiyan is not recommended.

However, Jiyan does have two advantages if he’s already on your account: He’s Quickswap-friendly, and he doesn’t need limited teammates to get close to his full potential. Sure, both Iuno and Ciaccona are upgrade paths, but Mortefi and Shorekeeper or Verina can suffice for clearing scores in low ToA floors or in Endstate Matrix. Don’t count on him for Whimpering Wastes though; despite his AoE capabilities, he doesn’t deal the damage required to keep up anymore. 

There are two issues still: First, the elephant in the room, there are a lot of characters who can accomplish this other than Jiyan. Good examples of this are Jingran, Suoming, Augusta and so on. Even in the free character department, Encore and Havoc Rover can work decently with free teammates, to a degree that approaches Jiyan’s. But they’re permanently available and don’t require a limited weapon to perform, unlike him.

Second, he pretty much cannot hit airborne enemies, and mobile enemies hurt his damage potential a lot as well. Even in his few use cases, he’s limited in terms of what enemies he can actually attack properly, simply because his attacks don’t connect against a lot of enemies in the game.

In conclusion, while Jiyan is not a recommended pull currently, if he’s already on your account, you can still get some decent use out of him. In ToA or Endstate Matrix, he can still perform if you have him properly invested and some teammates available (which shouldn’t be difficult as he has a good selection of free and limited teammates).
profile.pros:
• Strong AoE: Constant hits, and all Ultimate attacks group enemies;

  • One of the lowest Ultimate cooldowns in the game (16s) enable uniquely fast team rotations as his Ultimate allows him to access the majority of his damage;

  • Has good synergies with general buffers for Aero and Heavy Attack damage alike, as well as general Supports.
profile.cons:
• One of the oldest DPS characters in the game. Noticeably powercrept since release, struggles to clear endgame content when it becomes any difficult;

  • Signature weapon is basically necessary for him to clear any important endgame nowadays;

  • Can experience noticeable Energy issues depending on the enemy encounter and rotation used;

  • Almost incapable of hitting airborne enemies at all, strongly dislikes enemies with high mobility. Result: Jiyan straight-up doesn’t function against a lot of boss enemies in the game.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Jiyan’s main rotation goal is to enter Qingloong mode as quickly as possible through his Ultimate and get off as many Qingloong attacks as possible within that window. All of Jiyan’s rotation rely upon Dash Cancelling his Qingloong attacks to fire them off faster (as they deal about the same amount of damage as doing his full Qingloong attack chain, if not slightly more).

Echo Timing

Summon Nightmare: Feilian Beringal at any point in his rotation (Sierra Gale) or skip out on transforming into Nightmare: Kelpie entirely (Windward Pilgrimage).

In all the rotations below, Jiyan’s Qingloong attacks are Dash Cancelled to save on rotation time. This is the most basic rotation optimization he has access to. However, if cancelled too early, most of the hits will be interrupted. To prevent this, make sure to dash out of a Qingloong attack once Jiyan actually throws the dragon he summoned at the opponent (at that point, the hits will connect by themselves even if dashed out of).

Standard Rotation

The simplest rotation Jiyan has access to. Straightforward Hypercarry rotation that aims to get as many Qingloong attacks off as possible in his Ultimate window, disregarding Quickswap-related optimizations.

  • Intro

  • Ultimate: Finale

  • Basic: Lance of Qingloong 1 (Interrupt animation instantly via Skill)

  • Skill

  • Basic: Lance of Qingloong 1 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash then Skill) (7-8 times)

  • Skill (Swap)

  • Outro

While it's theoretically possible to execute an 8th full Qingloong within this rotation (casting a full Qingloong before your first Skill helps), it is very difficult and unrealistic due to enemies being able to interrupt you, and the timing being very tight. However, if you time a Tune Break Skill cast to act as a faster cancel than a Dash, it becomes a lot more possible (the timing becomes more lenient by about 0.4s, so against the least aggressive enemies in the game it becomes more realistic).

Double Intro

If your team has too much rotation time to spare, as Jiyan’s Ultimate cooldown is 16s but that may not be the case for most of his Supports who have longer cooldowns, Jiyan can spend extra time dealing some damage and restoring Energy for himself through a Double Intro rotation, like so:

  • Intro 

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack: Banner of Triumph

  • Skill (Swap)

→ Build up your Outro from your secondary character here.

  • Intro

  • Ultimate: Finale

  • Basic: Lance of Qingloong 1 (Interrupt animation instantly via Skill)

  • Skill

  • Basic: Lance of Qingloong 1 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash then Skill) (7 times)

  • Skill (Swap)

  • Outro

Additional Tips & Tricks

Jiyan is a fully Quickswap-friendly character. His teammates may not necessarily be Quickswap-friendly on their end, however in the case that they are (in a team like Ciaccona+Shorekeeper for example where no buffs expire on Swap), Jiyan is capable of Swap Cancelling each and every single one of his Qingloong attacks for other teammates to do their own rotations during Jiyan’s. For example, Ciaccona can chain a bunch of Jump → Plunge → Basic 4 combos and execute extra Forte Heavies in turn, as Jiyan is busy doing his own rotation.

Finally, Jiyan can rotate multiple times within Verina or Shorekeeper’s main buff windows thanks to his 16s-long Ultimate cooldown. In Quickswap with other fast rotation characters like Mortefi, it’s possible for Jiyan to rotate twice per full team loop, increasing his damage substantially. This is however limited to Quickswap as without it, he cannot save enough team rotation time for this to be worth it usually.

skills.name: Lone Lance
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 5 consecutive attacks, dealing Aero DMG.

Heavy Attack

Consume Stamina to perform a thrust attack, dealing Aero DMG.

Heavy Attack: Windborne Strike

Hold the Basic Attack during Heavy Attack to cast Windborne Strike after the Heavy Attack ends, dealing Aero DMG.

Heavy Attack: Abyssal Slash

Release the Basic Attack during the Heavy Attack to cast Abyssal Slash after the Heavy Attack ends, dealing Aero DMG.

Mid-air Attack

Consume Stamina to perform a Mid-Air Plunging Attack, dealing Aero DMG. After the Plunging Attack, use Basic Attack to perform a following attack, dealing Aero DMG.

Mid-air Attack: Banner of Triumph

After casting the Heavy Attack Windborne Strike or the Resonance Skill Windqueller in the air, Jiyan can perform an aerial attack, dealing Aero DMG.

Dodge Counter

Use a Basic Attack after a successful Dodge to attack the target with, dealing Aero DMG.

skills.name: Windqueller
skills.description: Dash forward a certain distance, dealing Aero DMG. Can be cast in the air.

skills.name: Emerald Storm: Prelude
skills.description:
After releasing Emerald Storm: Prelude, Jiyan enters Qingloong Mode.

Qingloong Mode

Jiyan has increased Anti-interruption; Basic Attack, Heavy Attack and Dodge Counter are replaced with Heavy Attack Lance of Qingloong.

Heavy Attack: Lance of Qingloong

Perform up to 3 continuous attacks, dealing Aero DMG, considered as Heavy Attack damage.

skills.name: Qingloong at War
skills.description:
When casting Resonance Skill Windqueller, if Jiyan has 30 or more "Resolve", he consumes 30 "Resolve" to increase the damage of this Resonance Skill Windqueller by 20%. When Jiyan is in Qingloong Mode, DMG of Resonance Skill Windqueller is increased by 20% and no longer consumes "Resolve".

Resonance Liberation: Emerald Storm: Finale

When casting Resonance Liberation Emerald Storm: Prelude, if Jiyan has 30 "Resolve" or more, he will consume 30 "Resolve" to cast Emerald Storm: Finale, dealing Aero DMG, considered as Heavy Attack damage. Emerald Storm: Finale can be cast in mid-air at low altitude.

Resolve

Jiyan can hold up to 60 Resolve. Jiyan gains "Resolve" when his Normal Attack Lone Lance hits the target. Jiyan gains "Resolve" when the Intro Skill Tactical Strike hits the target. If Jiyan does not hit a target within 15 seconds, his "Resolve" will gradually decrease.

skills.name: Discipline
skills.description: When the next Character's (or other Characters on a nearby team that activates an Outro Skill) Heavy Attack hits the target, Jiyan will summon Qingloong to launch a Coordinated Attack, dealing Aero DMG equal to 313.40% of Jiyan's ATK. This attack lasts for 8s, and can be triggered once every 1s, up to 2 times.

Resonance Liberation Emerald Storm: Finale will consume all "Momentum", and each stack consumed increases the DMG multiplier of Resonance Liberation Emerald Storm: Finale by 120%.

weapons.Comment: Jiyan's Signature is naturally his best weapon, as it grants him high Base ATK, alongside a lot of DMG Bonus to his main damage type being Heavy Attacks, and a CRIT DMG secondary stat to boot. A good blend of stats for a big damage increase compared to other weapons.
Augusta's Signature provides Jiyan with a massive Base ATK, a small CRIT Rate boost and some Heavy DMG. Not quite as good as his own Signature but still a very nice weapon to use on him.
Some general DMG Bonus with an emphasis on Skill DMG, alongside solid ATK and CRIT Rate stats make this weapon a solid choice on Jiyan.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Jiyan, who does not benefit from this weapon's Liberation DMG-focused effects.

Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Jiyan, who does not benefit from this weapon's Liberation DMG-focused effects - but funnily enough, it can buff Mortefi's damage if he's in Jiyan's team (it does not change this weapon's level of strength though).
Best permanently available option for Jiyan, which acts as a simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for him.

Best 4-star choice Jiyan has, this Battle Pass exclusive grants him a super easy-to-activate ATK and Heavy DMG passive effect alongside nice ATK and CRIT DMG stats, but its lower Base ATK makes it pale in comparison to most 5-stars.
Weakest 5-star choice that doesn't grant CRIT from its stats but instead focuses on higher ATK and some Energy Regen. Still viable for Jiyan, but not favoured over above options.
This Battle Pass exclusive grants Jiyan some scaling ATK and some CRIT Rate, which is acceptable but not recommended over 5-star choices due to its weak Base ATK.
Strongest no-gacha weapon for most Broadblade characters, granting a lot of ATK particularly if Negative Statuses are present on the enemy, but not recommended over 5-star choices.

echoes.Comment: Best set for Aero Main DPS characters who can apply Aero Erosion or have an Aero Erosion applier on the team. Grants 10% Aero DMG Bonus and an extra 30% Aero DMG Bonus as well as 10% CRIT Rate for 10s when attacking targets inflicted with Aero Erosion. Offers an extra 10% CRIT Rate over the other Aero sets such as Gusts of Welkin or Sierra Gale, providing extra overall damage so long as Aero Erosion is present on the enemy. In teams without Aero Erosion appliers however, this set is useless comparatively to Sierra Gale.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: This Echo provides a free decent amount of Aero DMG when casting Outro Skill in all situations, provides 12% Aero DMG Bonus to Jiyan and while its Transform Active Skill is not used in Jiyan's rotations, it is the best Main Echo he has, albeit by a very small difference when compared to Reminiscence: Fleurdelys (pick what has the best substats overall!)

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Aero DMG% boost and an additional 30% Aero DMG% after using the intro lasting 15 seconds for a grand total of 40% additional Aero damage for Jiyan's damage window.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Offers an unconditional 12% Aero DMG and Heavy ATK boost when used as the Main Echo, and additionally is a Summon-type echo making it easy to use in any character's rotation, which often makes it the best option for any character using the set.
echoes.Echo_2_Comment: Gives the same buffs as its Nightmare variant, but only after being transformed into, for a duration of 15 seconds. This Echo compensates by dealing close to double the damage of the Nightmare and giving more Energy to the character using it, but it's more difficult to incorporate into rotations, as it needs to be Swap Cancelled after the first hit to be used smoothly while making sure your character gets its buffs.

echoStats.Name: jiyan
echoStats.Substats: Energy Regen (Until Satisfied) > CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > ATK% > ATK = Heavy DMG%
echoStats.Comments: Always privilege Aero/ATK in compositions with Ciaccona, otherwise Aero/Aero can be equal to it.

skillPriority.Order: Res. Liberation, Forte Circuit, Res. Skill, Intro Skill, Basic Attack
skillPriority.Comments: Intro and Basic can be skipped when levelling to save on resources at a minimal damage loss.

teams.Name: Best Team
teams.Comments: Only consider Ciaccona in the third slot with Jiyan on Windward Pilgrimage, Iuno in the team, and Ciaccona on her Signature Weapon.

teams.Name: Erosion team
teams.Comments: Very strong in quickswap with Shorekeeper, can be equal to Jiyan's strongest team; Aero Rover is recommended for more casual players.

teams.Name: Lynae Team
teams.Comments: Only consider this team if Lynae and Mornye can't go anywhere else and Iuno isn't available - otherwise it may be a waste to spend such a strong universal buffing duo on Jiyan who has access to strong, free and permanent teammates.

synergies.Comment: As a Heavy Attack Main DMG dealer, Jiyan can function with a variety of Heavy Attack DMG buffers to increase his damage, Iuno being the best overall as she provides the best mix of buffs and personal damage as well as an Aero element synergy. Phrolova is an excellent Dual DPS option who also mixes in some Heavy DMG buffing, while Rebecca and Mortefi are the more accessible Heavy DMG buffing options accessible for free.

These two are more unconventional buffer choices for Jiyan. Ciaccona can either work as an insanely strong secondary in Quickswap Jiyan compositions as none of her buffs expire upon swapping, which means Jiyan can switch in the middle of his Heavy Attacks for Ciaccona to do several complete attack combos while Jiyan is rotating. However, for more casual players, Ciaconna is also undeniably the best third slot teammate for Jiyan alongside Iuno, making for a strong Mono Aero team composition. Lynae is also a possible option alongside Mornye as the duo's generalist buffing potential is enough to outdo any F2P team choices, but will see rarer use as that duo is often better used elsewhere.

Jiyan works with all kinds of universal Support options. Shorekeeper and Verina are the most obvious picks as they offer a wide variety of generalist, non-specialized buffs that can increase the entire team's damage regardless of who they are. Mornye and Aero Rover are more niche, as Mornye will only see use alongside Rebecca and Lynae for Hack and Tune Rupture synergies respectively, while Aero Rover may be considered alongside Ciaccona outside of Quickswap compositions for an Aero Erosion synergy.
